title: Which harness gets the most accepted work per dollar on the same model?
hypothesis: With the model held fixed, a minimal harness (pi) matches the heavier ones (opencode, native omo, fx) on accepted rate at a lower cost per accepted task.
human_gate: Frank approves installing any new harness on a machine; the container is the default place.

runs_on.why: Isolated scratch container. Keeps new harnesses and their telemetry off the YELLOW-zone laptop.

success_rule: A challenger replaces opencode as the worker default only if accepted_rate is within 5 points of opencode and cost_per_accepted is at least 20% lower.
kill: Stop at $8 or when one arm cannot run headless with the Gateway key (record that as a result). Any arm that sends telemetry we could not disable is dropped.

next_gate.receipt: lab/results/EXP-002.md harness table plus install provenance notes

decision_it_feeds: Which harness the cloud worker runs, and which one oh-my-starlight targets first.
preconditions: Install omo from a pinned package (bun add omo-ai@<version>), not the curl-pipe-shell installer.
Set OMO_SEND_ANONYMOUS_TELEMETRY=0 and OMO_DISABLE_POSTHOG=1; do not run omo setup against a config holding live keys.
Confirm native omo has a headless mode and can use an OpenAI-compatible Gateway endpoint (open issues 8815, 6813). If not, that is the result.

prior_evidence.claim: One vendor benchmark on DeepSeek V4 Flash found pi passed 20 of 30 tasks against oh-my-pi at 17 of 30, at about a quarter of the cost per success.
prior_evidence.source: Composio blog on pi vs omp
prior_evidence.caveat: Vendor blog, one model, 30 tasks. It motivates the test only.
